judged_text: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` accept arbitrary public input with no clamping and flow straight into `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` on the public members endpoint. Any logged-in user can pass `?limit=-1` (or a negative offset) and PostgreSQL rejects the query with 'LIMIT must not be negative', turning the public endpoint into a 500; a huge limit also re-opens the unbounded member materialization this PR was meant to close.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes them directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. From the diff alone, a request like `?limit=-1` or a negative `offset` would produce an invalid SQL `LIMIT/OFFSET` for PostgreSQL (commonly raising an error such as “LIMIT must not be negative”), turning the public endpoint into a 500. Likewise, a very large `limit` can force large materialization/response, undermining the pagination intent. This behavior is clearly present in the shown code path.
